messages:
leila: Heads up — onboarding bug: sampleapp README is unclear about where devs should keep API keys. Some of our examples use REDWOOD_KEY, others REDWOOD_API_KEY. This tripped up a new hire in Codespaces this morning. Are we recommending env vars only, or should we document a project-level creds file?

matt: We historically recommended REDWOOD_API_KEY in docs, but some older sampleapps and the local CLI creds file use different names (.redwood/credentials.json). There's definitely a docs/SDK parity gap.

sara: ugh, found it — sampleapp/.env.example still uses REDWOOD_KEY. that's the root cause for a few folks.

kumar: Proposal: standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY + optional REDWOOD_PROJECT. Fallback order for SDKs and CLI should be: env vars > CLI creds file (~/.config/redwood/credentials.json) > SDK profile. We should document the exact precedence and surface a warning when multiple keys are present.

leila: Can we do a small patch: (1) update sampleapp .env.example to REDWOOD_API_KEY and add REDWOOD_PROJECT comment, (2) update onboarding docs to show fallback order, (3) add a runtime SDK warning when ambiguous vars exist? Also ping SDK owners for parity.

matt: SDK implementation note: if both REDWOOD_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY present, prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY and emit a single warning: \"both REDWOOD_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY found — using REDWOOD_API_KEY. Please migrate.\" We should add the same behavior in JS/Python/Go SDKs. I'll open an interop issue.

jen: I can PR the sampleapp .env + README change today. sample snippet to include in README:

```
# .env.example
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-***    # preferred: per-developer API key
REDWOOD_PROJECT=my-product  # optional: project scope used by CLI & SDKs
```

tim: I'll file the sdk-interop issue and add a unit test suggestion for fallback ordering. @kumar please assign.

devex-bot: created issue #454 in repo sdk-interop: \"Normalize credential env vars and fallback order\" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-interop/issues/454

leila: Thanks everyone — this will reduce onboarding friction. target: patch before next cohort starts. :thumbsup:
